rawFindings.title: Formatted string responses lose UTF-8 charset
rawFindings.explanation: `res.format()` now sets `Content-Type` to only the normalized MIME type. Because `res.send()` does not add a charset when `Content-Type` is already present, text formats selected through `res.format()` are sent as `text/plain` or `text/html` without `charset=UTF-8`, even though Express encodes JavaScript strings as UTF-8. This regresses the previous behavior for non-ASCII formatted responses.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore appending the default charset for MIME types that have one, e.g. look up `mime.charsets.lookup(type)` and append `; charset=...` before setting `Content-Type`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: A route using `res.format({ text: function(){ res.send('café'); } })` with `Accept: text/plain` now responds with `Content-Type: text/plain` and a UTF-8 body; clients that follow the HTTP default for text without a charset can decode it incorrectly as ISO-8859-1, displaying `cafÃ©`.
